newsitem.title: UK: Visa used for record $1.0 trillion sales in year.
newsitem.headline: Visa used for record $1.0 trillion sales in year.

text.p: Visa International, the world's biggest consumer payments system, said on Monday its cards were used to buy a record $1.0 trillion in goods and services in the year to March 31.
The total was 23.7 percent higher than the $824 billion of purchases seen in the previous year.
Visa said that debit cards, which transfer money directly from a customer's bank account, rather than credit cards, which draw on a credit line, are the fastest growing part of its business.
Debit card transactions grew 40 percent in the latest year to $305 billion with a total of 119 million cards in use, a rise of 36.7 percent.
Total Visa cards in issue rose by 12.8 percent to March 31 with 572 million cards in use.
Visa president and CEO Edmund Jensen said smart cards could account for a third of its card base within five years. It already has 20 million smart cards in use.
It recently launched a multiple function smart card which is expected to lead to a major breakthrough in smart card usage.
Visa faces competition from the other major international payments consortium MasterCard in both smart card and electronic purse technology.
Visa's "Visa Cash" is up against MasterCard's link with Mondex International and others in the electronic purse and other markets.
